previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder in recovery, and depression presented with nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia. She was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis likely triggered by a urinary tract infection. She was treated in the emergency department with IV fluids, an insulin drip, and ceftriaxone. After stabilization, she was admitted to the medicine service, transitioned back to her home insulin regimen, and completed a short course of oral antibiotics. Her condition improved rapidly, with resolution of DKA and stable vital signs. She was discharged home with instructions to continue insulin, complete antibiotics, and follow up with her primary care provider and specialists within one week.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ y/o woman with a PMH notable for T1DM c/b 
DKA, alcohol abuse, HTN, depression, and anemia, who presented 
with N/V/D and hyperglycemia found to be in DKA. 

# DKA/DM1 uncontrolled: Patient has a history of type I diabetes 
with multiple admissions for DKA in the past.  She presented 
with n/v, diarrhea consistent with previous admissions. Noted to 
have an anion gap of 37 and a pH of 6.9 on admission. FSBG of 
700. Cause of DKA most likely due to not taking sliding scale 
insulin in the setting of not having access to glucometer vs. 
___ EtOH use.  Infectious workup unremarkable. EKG showed TWI 
(new compared to ___ and troponin is at 0.02, raising the 
possibility of ischemia. However, these findings are likely 
demand induced given her acidemia and stress state rather than 
the inciting event. She was started on an insulin gtt, and given 
aggressive hydration with close monitoring. Her glargine was 
given and she was able to tolerate a meal. Her insulin gtt was 
stopped and she was transferred out of the ICU. She was 
transitioned to long-acting glargine and was stable at the time 
of discharge. 

# Demand ischemia: 
TWI in V1-V3 new since ___. Troponin 0.02 but remained the 
same on repeat. Likely demand ischemia in the setting of stress 
from DKA as noted above. She remained on her home ASA and 
atorvastatin without further interventions. 
 
# ETOH Dependence/Abuse: 
Patient with noted EtOH abuse in the past, more consistent with 
binge drinking pattern rather than daily EtOH use. Autonomically 
stable upon arrival and without signs of active withdrawal. 
Thus, phenobarb was deferred and she was monitored on a CIWA 
scale, but never scored. She was given thiamine and folic acid. 
A social work consult was made. 

# Acute renal failure:
Cr 1.5 on admission up from baseline of 0.5-0.9.Most likely 
pre-renal in the setting of DKA and hypovolemia. Cr downtrending 
with IVF and urine sodium < 10 consistent with prerenal 
azotemia.  Cr had normalized by the time of discharge. 

# Leukocytosis: 
Resolved. Likely a stress response as infectious work up 
negative and patient without localizing symptoms. 

# Depression
Continued home dose mirtazapine and venlafaxine.
